title: Seolleongtang
subtitle: korean milky beef bone soup
excerpt: Seolleongtang is a Korean soup made from a long-simmered beef broth that turns milky and rich from the collagen in the bones. It is served plain with rice, spring onion, and seasoning on the side. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Seolleongtang has been made in Korea since the Joseon era. It is one of the few Korean soups that arrives at the table completely unseasoned, allowing each diner to season it themselves.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the broth in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen over medium heat.
recipe.batchNotes: The broth keeps for 5 days in the fridge. Skim the fat from the surface when cold before reheating.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a day ahead so the fat can be skimmed from the cold surface.

glossaryTerms.definition: A protein found in bones, cartilage, and connective tissue. When simmered for a long time, collagen dissolves and gives stock a rich, silky body. It turns cloudy and milky in seolleongtang.
Small Korean side dishes served alongside a main meal. They sit at the centre of the table and are shared between all diners.

content.text: Seolleongtang gets its characteristic milky colour from
dissolving from the bones into the broth during several hours of boiling. The result is a deeply nourishing, mild soup. Serves 4.
This recipe uses good quality beef stock as the base and beef sirloin for the meat, giving a flavour close to the original without the need for bones. Serve with plenty of

items.prepNote: ground, to serve at the table

content.text: Combine the beef stock, water, beef sirloin, garlic, ginger, and onion in a stockpot. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam. Reduce to a steady simmer.
Simmer for 1.5 hours with the lid on, then remove the lid and increase the heat to a moderate boil. Boil for a further 45 minutes. This emulsifies the fat into the broth and creates the milky colour.
Remove the beef from the broth. Once cool enough to handle, shred it thinly with your fingers or a fork.
Strain the broth through a sieve and discard the aromatics. Return the broth to the pot and bring back to a gentle simmer. Taste and add a pinch of fine sea flakes if needed.

Place a portion of cooked rice in each bowl. Add the shredded beef. Ladle the hot broth over the top. Serve with spring onion, black pepper, and sesame oil on the side for each person to season their own bowl.

attrs.fix: The heat is too low. Turn it up to a moderate boil during the last 45 minutes. The turbulence is what emulsifies the fat into the broth.
Simmer for longer. Seolleongtang beef needs extended cooking. Add 30 more minutes and check again.
Season only at the table with fine flakes and black pepper. Seolleongtang is intentionally mild from the pot. The seasoning is added by each person.

content.text: Seolleongtang restaurants in Seoul open early and serve from morning until night. The soup is a popular breakfast in Korea. It is one of the oldest street foods in the city. The broth takes hours to make so it is usually left on the heat overnight. Each bowl arrives plain and seasoning is personal.
